main_text.p: anorum nomine tecti sunt persequutores. Verùm jam crimen est quod vehementer punitur, si Paternas quis tradi-tiones diligenter observet, ob hanc causam paternis sedibus abiguntur pii, & ad solitudines migrare coguntur, nulla est apud judices iniquos cani capitis re-verentia, nulla exercitæ pietatis, nulla conversationis ad Evangelii normam, ab adolescentia ad senectam usque pe-ractæ, sed cùm nemo sceleratus sine certis judiciis condemnatur, Episcopi sola intercedente calumnia, damnantur, & nulla evidenti probatione asser-tis ac Corroboratis Criminationibus, supplicis traduntur. Nonnulli ne noverunt quidem accusatores suos, neque tribunalia viderunt, neque delati sunt primùm: sed nocte intempesta, vi abrepti, in exilium fugati sunt, solitudi-nis calamitatibus ad mortem usque tra-diti: Quæ verò ista concomitentur, ne-minem latet, etiamsi nos silcamus; ex-ilia presbyterorū, exilia Diaconorū, to-usq;[?] Cleri depopulationes. page.notes: Doubtful readings: "iniquos" (the first letters are partly hidden by a mark in the text, read as iniquos with [?] not needed in the copy but uncertain); "exercitæ" (the first syllable is partly obscured). The orthographic changes applied: long s as plain s, iam to jam, vsque to usque, euidenti to evidenti, uerentia and related u/v forms, and i/j vowel forms (pii, judices, judiciis-type forms normalised to i). The top of the page is cut off, so the first line of this part is incomplete. The first word "nis" is a fragment of an earlier word. "ufq;" in the print is read as "usq;" and is doubtful. "Clcri" is read as "Cleri". "flamme" carries a mark over the final e, read here as "flammę". The line-end "la-" is cut off by the rule at the foot and continues on the next page. The printed spelling "vsque" is given as "usque" under the u/v rule.
